title: Traffic calming overhaul and speed management update
subtitle: Columbia Street speed limit cut, lease renewals, camp subsidy agreement, drinking water reports and deferred items.
overview: Council approved a new Traffic Calming and Collision Countermeasure Program {{vote:m9}}. It replaces the traffic calming policy in the 2011 Transportation Master Plan. Staff plan to use large speed and connected-vehicle data sets to find problem locations across the whole city, rather than relying on short counts at single sites. They expect this to shorten the time from a request to installation.

Council also received the 2024 speed management update and approved a speed limit reduction to 50 km/h on Columbia Street between Phillip Street and Erbsville Road {{vote:m8}}. Traffic and Parking By-law amendments were updated to match. Staff said the change can go ahead once the by-law is in force and utility locates are done for the new signs.

A consent group of items was also approved. It included the 2023 drinking water reports {{vote:m3}}, two Waterloo City Centre lease renewals {{vote:m5}} {{vote:m6}}, and a service agreement with the Region for subsidized children's camp fees {{vote:m7}}. A report on surplus land on Millennium Blvd and a public meeting on a rezoning at 251 Albert Street were both deferred to later dates. Notices of motion were given for March 4 on the Ontario Heritage Act and the Ontario Energy Board.

decisions.detail: Council replaced the 2011 Transportation Master Plan traffic calming policy with a new data-driven Traffic Calming and Collision Countermeasure Program.
Council reduced the speed limit on Columbia Street between Phillip Street and Erbsville Road to 50 km/h and updated the Traffic and Parking By-law, in line with Vision Zero.
Council received the 2023 annual and summary drinking water reports under Ontario Regulation 170/03 and approved report IPPW2024-007.
Council approved the lease renewal for Advanis Inc. at the Waterloo City Centre and authorized the Mayor and Clerk to sign the amending agreement.
Council approved the lease renewal for the Member of Parliament's office at the Waterloo City Centre and authorized signing of the amending agreement.
Council approved a service agreement with the Region of Waterloo for subsidized camp fees for children and related camp subsidy agreements.

debate: On speed management, councillors said the data showed average speeds in the study areas falling below 40 km/h and the fastest drivers slowing noticeably. One councillor said lowering limits gave the broadest behaviour change of any calming tool.

Councillors asked about outliers in the school-zone data. Staff had no explanation for one school and would keep monitoring it. Another school area still had speeding concerns, and staff said posted limits are one tool, with more measures to follow.

Councillors raised speed cameras in school zones as another tool, citing one school zone where speeds and traffic volumes dropped. A councillor also noted that the Region is looking at speeding on Regional roads.

On the new program, councillors asked how individual resident requests would be handled. Staff said they would respond faster with citywide priority data, urgent items such as no-parking signs would be handled as now, and engagement with residents and school groups would continue.

Councillors asked about data limits and privacy. Staff said connected-vehicle data records speed and hard braking or acceleration, not the type of road user or licence plates. Staff said privacy rules and agreements would apply, and a federal grant application and vendor procurement are still pending.
